Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API: upcoming renewal + throughput planning

Hi Avery,

Our renewal for the Hosted API subscription is up in mid-January. Our consumption has steadily increased after the November feature launch and we expect the same cadence through Q2 next year. We're exploring increasing our monthly commit and moving into a higher usage tier to smooth latency during promotional spikes.

Can you share what a path to a higher commit looks like on your side? Specifically:
- Typical uplift cadence (step-ups vs. single commit bump)
- Pricing bands for 2x and 3x current monthly commits
- Burst / soft-throttle behavior for traffic spikes
- Any recommended model/quantization profiles to lower unit cost for our query mix

I've attached our last two months of usage for reference. cc'd procurement (procure@acme.com) for the contract side.

Would like to schedule a call—Jill / Marcus O'Neal (platform) / procurement—sometime this week.

Thanks,
Jill Park
Head of ML Platform, Acme Retail
[Attachment: acme_usage_dec_nov.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: upcoming renewal + throughput planning

Hi Jill — thanks for the data and the heads up. Happy to take this on.

High level intake:
- We can support either a stepped commit ladder (quarterly step-ups) or a one-time commit increase. Step-ups give you better price smoothing; a single bump is simpler operationally.
- For 2x commit we typically recommend moving to the Tier B rate band; for 3x we propose Tier C with a small per-token discount and guaranteed burst buffer. I'll pull exact rate numbers and send a formal proposal.
- Burst behavior: soft-throttle kicks in after committed throughput + burst pocket. We can configure a temporary grace for promotional windows.
- Ops: we strongly recommend enabling prefix KV caching for your top 200 templates and the quantization profile we ran in staging (q4_8) — that reduces unit cost ~18% on your mix.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Quick call to align requirements & SLAs (30 min) — available Thu 11–12 PT or Fri 9–11 PT
2) Redwood to send a proposal + amendment (includes proposed commit, tier, burst credits, per-token rate)
3) Procurement review + redlines (procurement contact cc'd)
4) Execute amendment via DocuSign and lock in new commit

I'll loop Ben for pricing details and Lauren for the DocuSign flow.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
